title: JANUS Linear A fresh transcription/parser source candidate provenance audit
audit_question: Which available Linear A source is sufficiently independent in transcription/editorial encoding and sufficiently machine-accessible to support a genuinely new source-specific parser and later locked external-replication replay?

not_sufficient: different frontend over the same structured transcription
copy of mwenge/lineara.xyz tokenization or word-break decisions
required_or_strongly_preferred: separately maintained/editorially curated transcription or sign-instance encoding
documented provenance to printed editions or artifact inspection
independent sign/word-boundary/editorial decisions or a route that allows us to derive them independently
machine-readable data or a feasible source-specific normalization path
numeric and punctuation conventions documented well enough to rebuild the typed-token ontology without mwenge-specific assumptions
license/access terms compatible with reproducible research
explicit demonstration of dependency relationships before claiming external replication

documented_pipeline: The LinearA Explorer README states that George Douros produced a spreadsheet tabulating documents with word breaks, ideograms and numerals.
The spreadsheet was converted through CSV into the structured LinearAInscriptions.js data used by the explorer.
The project also uses GORILA images/transcriptions as the principal epigraphic foundation and separately incorporates John Younger's commentaries.
current_mwenge_baseline_provenance.independence_consequence: A future source must not be treated as external merely because it republishes GORILA or Younger if it imports the same Douros/mwenge structured transcription decisions.

candidates.name: SigLA — The Signs of Linear A: a paleographical database
candidates.license: Dataset and drawings advertised under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 on the official site.
provenance_evidence: SigLA is maintained by Salgarella and Castellan as a separate open-access paleographical database.

The project paper describes creation of their own drawings of documents from the standard printed corpus, separation of individual signs into Krita layers, individual sign classification and epigraphic metadata assignment.
Their custom Import software converts the Krita corpus into a JSON database and generated document/sign images.
The interface is custom software rather than a wrapper around mwenge/lineara.xyz.
The official About page records continuing additions of documents, including updates in 2026.
shared_dependencies: SigLA explicitly draws substantially from the printed GORILA corpus, so it is not independent at the level of underlying published epigraphic evidence.
This shared GORILA dependency must be separated conceptually from independence of digital encoding/editorial sign-instance annotation.
dependency_not_found_but_not_proven_abse: No evidence has yet been found in the inspected official documentation that SigLA imports George Douros's spreadsheet, LinearAInscriptions.js, or mwenge tokenization.
Absence of such evidence is not proof of absence; source/data dependency audit remains open.

raw_access_state.blocker: Need an exact downloadable JSON/archive or source repository path before source-specific parser implementation can begin reproducibly.

what_would_promote_to_R3_PASS: Resolve the exact raw JSON/dataset or source-code repository path.
Verify the raw dataset can be obtained without passing through mwenge/lineara.xyz.
Inspect schema for document IDs, sign IDs, sign groups/word grouping, numerals, punctuation, uncertainty and variants.
Search source/import code and documentation for dependency on Douros, Younger structured exports or mwenge files.
Record an immutable source version/digest or repository commit.

candidates.name: Direct GORILA editions via Cefael / École française d'Athènes
provenance_evidence: Cefael exposes the five Godart/Olivier Recueil des inscriptions en Linéaire A volumes (GORILA I-V), including tablets, nodules, roundels, other documents and addenda/corrigenda/sign plates.
This route bypasses the George Douros spreadsheet and mwenge JSON conversion layer.
limitations: The inspected Cefael route is a digitized publication interface, not a ready machine-readable transcription dataset.
A JANUS parser would need a new transcription/normalization workflow derived from the editions themselves.
Because both mwenge and SigLA use GORILA heavily, direct GORILA is not independent at the underlying printed-edition level; its value is independence from downstream digital transcription decisions.
candidates.best_use: Reference/ground-truth route for provenance checking, disagreement adjudication and potentially a genuinely fresh transcription pipeline if a reproducible extraction method is built.

candidates.name: John Younger Linear A transliterations/commentaries
provenance_evidence: SigLA documentation describes Younger as providing online Linear A transliterations based on GORILA with improved/updated readings.
mwenge/lineara.xyz separately states that it incorporates John Younger's commentaries.
limitations: Younger is already inside the broader evidence ecosystem used by mwenge, so it is not a clean untouched external source for our present pipeline.
Its GORILA basis further reduces epigraphic-source independence.
candidates.best_use: Reading-disagreement audit or alternative-reading comparison, not primary external replication corpus.

candidates.name: The pa-i-to Linear A Epigraphic Project
provenance_evidence: The project explicitly describes its goal as publication of a new critical edition of the Linear A documents from Phaistos.
It is a paleo-epigraphic/philological project involving Sapienza Università di Roma, Heraklion Archaeological Museum and other institutional partners.
The project documents 48 Phaistos Linear A objects and reports active digitalization and study, including 2D+/3D models.
limitations: Coverage is site-specific and cannot replace a broad corpus for all-region replication.
The inspected public pages do not yet establish a downloadable machine-readable full transcription/sign-instance dataset.
Digital model licensing is scientific/non-profit with rights restrictions rather than the clearly reusable dataset licensing seen on SigLA.
candidates.best_use: High-value independent site-specific validation source, especially for Phaistos, if structured transcription access can be obtained.

ranking.reason: Best combination currently observed of separate maintainers, custom sign-instance editorial pipeline, own drawings/classification, documented JSON generation, broad corpus scope and reusable dataset license. Raw access/dependency proof is the remaining gate.

Strongest route for bypassing downstream digital transcription layers, but requires creation of a new reproducible transcription/parser and still shares the foundational printed edition used by other corpora.
Potentially strong independent critical re-edition with object-level digital work, but presently site-limited and machine-readable transcription access is unconfirmed.
Useful alternate readings but not cleanly external because mwenge already incorporates Younger commentary and both are GORILA-based.

R3_gate_state.blocker: Resolve a reproducible raw SigLA dataset/source-code path and verify dependency independence from Douros/mwenge structured data.

next_actions.action: Resolve SigLA raw JSON/archive/source repository URL and freeze a version/digest.
Inspect SigLA schema and importer/source for Douros/Younger/mwenge dependencies and document sign-group/numeric/punctuation conventions.
If SigLA passes raw-access/dependency audit, create a source-specific parser under research/linear_a/ without importing mwenge parser assumptions.
Create a normalization-only receipt comparing document/sign coverage and disagreement structure before any external replication claim.
Freeze a later external-replication spec that replays locked controls/transforms rather than rediscovering candidates on the fresh source.
